featured_reviews.name: Shriraj Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing for a Place Known for Biryani

I visited this restaurant with high expectations because it’s known for its biryani, but unfortunately the experience was a big letdown.

We ordered:
Malai Tikka
Lollipop Masala
Large Chicken Dum Biryani

The Lollipop Masala was the only item that stood out. It was flavorful, almost like a Schezwan-style lollipop, and honestly the best part of the entire meal.

The Malai Tikka, however, was very disappointing. The chicken was rubbery, didn’t taste fresh, and despite decent presentation, the flavor and texture were not enjoyable at all.

Now coming to the main attraction - the Large Chicken Dum Biryani (around ₹600). For this price, getting only 3 pieces of chicken already felt underwhelming. The rice lacked the rich aroma and layered spices that you expect from a good dum biryani. There was barely any biryani masala, and while the chicken was technically well-cooked in dum style, it had very little flavor.

Overall, the biryani felt plain, dull, and nowhere close to what a place with “Biryani” in its name should serve.

What made it even more disappointing was that friends who had visited earlier said the food used to be much better - but this time none of us enjoyed it.

Final verdict:
For a restaurant called Biryani Darbar, the biryani does not live up to the name at all. I’m giving 2 stars only because of the Lollipop Masala. Everything else was far below expectations.

I really hope they improve the consistency and quality because right now, it does not justify the price or reputation.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Valued Customer,
Feedback noted. It would have been more helpful if you have informed Captain about the same and we would have checked and addressed this immediately. We truly believe in customer service. Also, there were no such complaints from any of our customers. We apologise for your experience and hope you allow us another chance to serve you better. Thank you.

featured_reviews.name: Suketu CHANDAN
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Biryani Darbar and it was an absolute delight!

Biryani here is easily one of the best I've had in Mumbai. Perfectly cooked long-grain rice, perfect vegetable masala and that rich, fragrant dum-cooked flavor with just the right balance of spicey, not too oily, not too dry, just perfect. The raita and salan that came with it were excellent accompaniments.

For desserts, I tried both Gajar Halwa and Shahi Tukda, and both were outstanding!
The Gajar Halwa was rich, moist, and packed with the natural sweetness of carrots, loaded with ghee, nuts, and khoya. It tasted completely homemade – warm, comforting, and indulgent.

Shahi Tukda was equally impressive – crispy fried bread soaked in fragrant saffron milk, topped with nuts and a touch of rose water. It had the perfect texture contrast and wasn't overly sweet. Both desserts felt luxurious and authentic.
The service was quick and friendly, and the portions were generous. Ambiance is simple but comfortable – perfect for a hearty meal with family or friends.

If you're a biryani lover or craving proper Mughlai desserts, Biryani Darbar Goregaon is a must-visit. Everything we ordered was top-notch. Easily one of the best biryani places in the area.

Highly recommended – 5 Stars! 🔥
Will definitely be going back soon.

featured_reviews.name: Asad Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Having always wanted to visit Lucky Restaurant, the legendary Bandra West institution famous for a Biryani so iconic it is famously loved by actor Salman Khan’s family, I was thrilled to try their brand-new branch in Goregaon East.
We started with the Chicken Manchow Soup, which was served remarkably hot and tasted fantastic with a rich, delicious, masala-based flavor, though a few unblended chunks occasionally disrupted the texture. Unfortunately, the Prawns Chilly starter was a letdown, featuring tiny, chewy prawns and an average sauce that we ultimately couldn't finish.
However, the highly anticipated Chicken Biryani completely redeemed the meal. It was absolutely perfect, boasting a flawless blend of spices, tender meat, and a delicious accompanying raita that made the whole visit worthwhile. We wrapped up with the Apricot Delight dessert, which was spectacularly flavorful and highly recommended.
Across the board, the portions were much larger than expected, justifying the slightly expensive pricing, and the service from the super nice staff was excellent. My only critique is that they should expand their soft drink menu beyond standard Pepsi and Coca-Cola to include options like Campa, Big Cola, and Lahori to better complement their heavy, flavorful dishes.

The dish was drowning in oil. My hands were literally covered with oil while eating, and even my throat got irritated afterward.
When I called the restaurant, instead of taking responsibility, they simply said, "Utna to hota hi hai" and started giving excuses.
This is not Khepsa — it's just oily fried rice loaded with excessive oil. The quality was terrible, the taste was disappointing, and the amount of oil used was ridiculous.
Extremely frustrated and disappointed. If this is the standard of food being served, customers deserve much better. Not recommended at all.

The service was equally disappointing. We requested a tissue refill four separate times, but no one seemed concerned enough to attend to it. The staff appeared inactive and inattentive throughout our visit.
Overall, both the food quality and service fell far below expectations. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and works on improving these aspects.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently dined at Lucky Restaurant and it turned out to be a delightful culinary experience.

We ordered the half Murg Mussallam, which came with two rich and flavorful gravies – one a vibrant yellow and the other a deep red. The dish was generously topped with juicy tandoori chicken pieces, making it both unique and hearty. Paired with butter garlic naan, the meal was absolutely satisfying and more than enough for two people.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian pudding, which was a real highlight – rich, creamy, and beautifully balanced in flavor. The caramel custard was just as expected – smooth and classic, a comforting end to the meal.

The service was prompt and courteous, and the prices were reasonable for the quality and portion size. A special shoutout to the kitchen for the thoughtful preparation and presentation.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for flavorful Non veg Indian dishes and comforting desserts in a relaxed setting.

I request you to investigate this incident, take strict corrective action, and ensure such negligence does not happen again. I also expect an appropriate response from your side regarding this matter

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our recent visit to Lucky Biryani turned out to be a delicious journey through rich Mughlai flavours, ending with some comforting desserts that rounded off the meal perfectly.

We ordered the Murg Musallam, and it was easily the highlight of our meal. A whole chicken, richly marinated and cooked in a thick, aromatic gravy made with a blend of spices, nuts, and cream – the dish was indulgent, flavorful, and felt true to its royal roots. The chicken was tender, infused with spices, and the gravy was luscious without being overly heavy. The quantity was more than sufficient for two to three people and extremely filling, making it great value for money.

To go along with it, we had Butter Garlic Naan – soft, perfectly cooked with a generous brush of butter and a strong hit of garlic that paired beautifully with the Musallam.

For dessert, we tried the Arabian Pudding, a milk-based sweet that was delicate and smooth, with hints of cardamom and saffron. It was light and refreshing after the rich main course.

We also had the Caramel Custard, which was classic and well-done – creamy, just the right amount of sweetness, and topped with a golden layer of caramel that melted on the tongue.

Overall, Lucky Biryani delivered a satisfying meal – flavour-packed, generously portioned, and rounded off with nostalgic desserts. A great spot if you’re in the mood for classic Mughlai fare done right.

featured_reviews.name: Ketan Choudhari
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited this restaurant, and I must say it turned out to be a delightful food experience. Each dish had its own character and flavor, making the meal memorable.
Starting with Chicken Tikka Masala with Naan, it was the highlight of the evening. The chicken was perfectly cooked – tender and juicy with that smoky flavor you expect from a good tikka. The masala gravy was rich, creamy, and just the right balance of spicy and tangy. Paired with the soft, buttery naan, it was comfort food at its finest. The naan was fluffy with crisp edges and complemented the curry beautifully.

Next, I tried Jeera Rice with Dal Tadka, and it felt like pure soul food. The jeera rice was fragrant, light, and well-cooked without being sticky. The dal tadka was flavorful with a perfect tempering of garlic, red chilies, and cumin. It wasn’t overly spicy, but packed with aroma and homely taste – exactly the kind of dish that makes you feel satisfied and content.

Finally, the Chole Bhature deserves special mention. The bhature were soft, fluffy, and not dripping with excess oil, while the chole had that authentic North Indian taste – spicy, tangy, and loaded with flavor. It’s the kind of dish that makes you want to order it again even when you’re full.

Overall, the food was consistently good across all dishes. The portion sizes were generous, and the service was prompt. A must-visit place if you’re craving authentic Indian flavors!

Contents: The dish features tender, bone-in chicken pieces that were cooked perfectly.

Sides: It came with raita on the side, which was fresh and paired beautifully with the rice.
Overall, a high-quality, authentic meal. I’d definitely recommend it if you’re looking for a flavorful, well-packaged biryani.

The ambience is average and the prices are also reasonable, maybe slightly on the higher side but I got value for money, so it seemed fair to me. They had steel chairs with no leather seats - they can improve on that.

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
Royal Challenge in Goregaon East has always carried an iconic reputation — a restaurant known for its history, warmth, and connection to Mumbai’s old glamour. The moment you step inside, you’re greeted by a wall of nostalgia — photographs of Bollywood celebrities from the 80s and 90s, capturing the era when this was the go-to spot for stars and elite patrons. The ambiance still reflects that classic charm — comfortable, elegant, and filled with stories of the city’s golden years.

The food, at first, absolutely lived up to expectations. Every dish we ordered tasted fresh, flavorful, and well-prepared. The seasoning was balanced, the portions generous, and the presentation impressive. It truly felt like a restaurant that takes pride in maintaining quality even after so many years in business. The service too was prompt, polite, and warm — the staff made us feel genuinely cared for, which added to the overall positive dining experience.

However, our experience took a disappointing turn the next morning. Out of five family members who dined together, three of us ended up with an upset stomach and loose motion. It’s unfortunate because, while the food tasted excellent, this after-effect raised questions about hygiene or food handling consistency.

It’s a restaurant that clearly has a glorious legacy, a top-notch ambiance, and courteous service, but maintaining strict kitchen hygiene is just as important as taste. I truly hope the management takes this feedback seriously, as Royal Challenge has the potential to remain a trusted classic — provided the focus on food safety matches the charm of its reputation.

Would still love to return someday — hopefully to the same great taste without the unpleasant aftermath.

customer_updates.text:
A Disappointing Thaali Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant left much to be desired, particularly concerning their thaali offerings. While some aspects were tolerable, several critical flaws made for a truly underwhelming experience.

1) Quantity Concerns
Practically all thaali options severely lack in quantity. What's served feels more like an appetizer than a substantial meal. Thaalis, if nothing else, should be known for their generous portions. The amount we received made us question if it was truly a thaali or merely a half-thaali (even though we didn't order the latter).

2) Quality and Ambiance
I won't heavily critique the quality of the food, as it wasn't outright bad, but let's just say it wholeheartedly embraces mediocrity.
As for the ambiance, the place tries too hard to mimic the rustic vibe of a Konkani Waada but fails miserably. Instead, it now resembles a poorly lit, questionable restaurant that seems better suited for unsavory characters.

3) Service Shortcomings
Perhaps it was an isolated incident, but the server assigned to our table struggled to speak clearly. We could barely hear him, making it impossible to communicate or inquire about the dishes. This wasn't a language barrier; it simply seemed he was disengaged from his job.
Furthermore, no server approached us to ask if we needed anything. It made us wonder if we were paying customers or if they were doing us a charity by feeding us for free.

4) Unacceptable Thaali Details
The thaali lacks essential condiments. The onions served on the side were poorly prepared, coming as huge, unappetizing chunks in a tiny bowl. Ideally, onion rings would be provided for ease of picking.

The charges for the thaali are absurdly high for the meager amount provided. I've attached a picture of the pomfret thaali; notice the fish was chopped instead of being served whole. What kind of thaali serves fish like this? It's as if they don't differentiate between a fish thaali and a fish starter, providing the same portion for both.

We were charged over ₹1000 for this thaali. I know at least 25 other places that offer a far better value pomfret thaali for around ₹800. I may sound like a broken record, but thaalis are supposed to be this place's unique selling point. Getting so many things wrong with them makes me question if they truly thought things through when they decided to feature thaalis prominently on their menu.

5) Staff Demeanor
The staff and management exude fake politeness. It's as if they resent working there or are simply disengaged.
A Personal Disappointment
To be fair, this next point is a bit personal and may not apply to everyone, but it's worth mentioning. Tonight was a special occasion for me (a Kelvan, a Marathi get-together for a groom-to-be). My friends brought a Baskin Robbins cake, and we simply asked if we could cut it there after our meal – we didn't ask them to prepare it. They refused us permission. How can a place charge so much per thaali and then deny customers the chance to acknowledge a special day? It felt as though this establishment actively discourages celebrations. What kind of business drives away potential sales by being unaccommodating to pre- and post-celebration arrangements?

6) Uncomfortable Seating
Finally, the seating arrangement was slightly uncomfortable. The tables were a bit too large, the chairs didn't prioritize comfort, and the sofas attached to the walls were old and thus uncomfortable.

featured_reviews.name: tejas thorat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the privilege of dining at The Maratha Kitchen, courtesy of our boss, who treated our team to a lunch outing. What started as a casual team lunch quickly turned into one of the most memorable Maharashtrian dining experiences I have had in recent times.

As someone from the hospitality industry and a passionate food enthusiast, I can confidently say that The Maratha Kitchen stands apart for its authenticity, consistency, and unwavering commitment to quality. Much of the credit goes to owner Abhishek Tulaskar, a passionate hotelier with extensive industry experience. His understanding of food, sourcing, and guest experience is evident in every aspect of the restaurant.

One thing that immediately impressed me was Abhishek's uncompromising approach towards the quality of mutton served. He is extremely selective about sourcing and accepts nothing short of the best. In an era where portion sizes are often shrinking, The Maratha Kitchen takes a refreshingly generous approach. Almost every mutton entrée contains nearly a quarter kilogram of mutton, ensuring diners receive both exceptional quality and outstanding value.

Our group of six largely opted for the Maratha Mutton Thali and Kolhapuri Mutton Thali, accompanied by Bombil Rawa Fry and Prawn Rawa Fry, Mutton kharda, Prawn agri masala.

The thalis are thoughtfully curated and offer a complete Maharashtrian culinary experience. Each thali includes Mutton Sukka, Mutton Rassa, Alni Rassa, Solkadhi, fragrant Indrayani Rice, and a choice between traditional Jowar Bhakri or rice bhakri and koshimbir.

The waiting time for the thalis was approximately 20-25 minutes, but the freshness and quality of preparation made the wait completely worthwhile.

The Bombil Rawa Fry deserves special mention. The bombil was expertly flattened, marinated beautifully, coated with rawa, and fried until perfectly crisp while retaining its delicate texture. The Prawn Rawa Fry was equally impressive, fresh, juicy, and packed with flavour.

Coming to the star attraction, the mutton.

The Mutton Sukka was robust and flavourful, showcasing a perfect balance of spices while allowing the quality of the meat to shine through. The Mutton Rassa was rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying. However, the true hero of the meal was undoubtedly the Alni Rassa. Often overshadowed by its spicier counterparts, this version was exceptional. Light yet intensely flavourful, it carried the essence of slow-cooked mutton stock and delivered remarkable depth and comfort with every spoonful.

The restaurant's Tambda Rassa and Pandhra Rassa are beautifully balanced. They provide enough spice and richness to excite the palate without overwhelming the natural flavour of the meat.

If there is one dish that every diner must order, it is unquestionably the Mutton Kharda.

In my opinion, it is one of the finest versions available in the city today. Despite being one of the simplest preparations on the menu, it was easily the most memorable dish of the afternoon. Tender pieces of mutton are slow-cooked in ghee and paired with freshly pounded green chilli thecha and turmeric. The meat is so tender that it effortlessly falls off the bone. The richness of the ghee beautifully complements the sharp heat of the chillies, creating a dish that is rustic, honest, and incredibly flavourful. Sometimes the simplest recipes produce the most unforgettable results, and this dish is proof of that.

Another standout was the Agri Prawns, tossed in a bold Agri-style masala and cooked with the shells intact to preserve maximum flavour. Every bite delivered an authentic coastal character that seafood lovers will appreciate.

After such a hearty and spice-forward meal, the desserts provided the perfect conclusion. The Peru Ice Cream was refreshing and unique, while the Narali Bhat Ice Cream brilliantly captured the essence of the traditional Maharashtrian sweet dish in frozen form. Both desserts acted as excellent palate cleansers and a fitting finale to the meal.

Rating: 4.8/5

featured_reviews.name: Prashant “Paddy” Demello
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a seafood lover in Mumbai and haven’t eaten at Nityananda Lunch Home in Goregaon East, you’re seriously missing out. Tucked away on a busy stretch, this humble joint has earned a legendary reputation among locals for serving affordable, flavorful, and authentic coastal cuisine. What makes Nityananda truly special is its inclusiveness — you’ll see everyone from daily wage workers to white-collar professionals eating side by side, enjoying the same spicy, satisfying food.

The restaurant specializes in Malvani, Konkani, and South Indian seafood, and the flavors are as real as it gets. Their seafood curries — especially the prawns curry, bangda curry, surmai gravy, and fish thalis — are packed with the kind of rustic, homestyle masalas that make you want to lick your fingers. The curries tend to be on the oilier side, but that’s part of the charm — it gives the dishes a rich, bold taste that’s hard to find in high-end restaurants.

I personally love their South Indian seafood curries — the balance of coconut, curry leaves, and tamarind is spot on. The fish is always fresh, and the portions are generous for the price. Even the simplest meal of rice and curry with a fried fish on the side feels hearty and fulfilling.

Yes, they offer home delivery and are available on Swiggy and Zomato, which is convenient — but to be honest, the real value comes from dining in. The rising delivery charges and taxes often end up making the same ₹200 meal cost ₹300+. Instead, walk into Nityananda, grab a seat, and enjoy a hot, freshly cooked meal served within minutes. The quick service, buzzing atmosphere, and strong smell of seafood and spices make the experience all the more memorable.

It’s not a fancy place by any means — simple tables, quick-moving staff, a menu that hasn’t changed in years — but it doesn’t need to be. The food speaks for itself. It’s no wonder Nityananda has such a strong base of loyal, repeat customers who keep coming back for comfort food that never fails.

If you’re in Goregaon East and looking for a budget-friendly, full-flavored seafood experience, Nityananda Lunch Home should be at the top of your list. It’s not just a restaurant — it’s a local treasure.

I ordered the paya soup and prawns biryani from here.

The prawns biryani was delicious. The prawns were fresh, well cooked, and had that subtle bite you expect, without being rubbery. The biryani rice was aromatic, well infused with masala, and flavorful throughout, making it a very enjoyable dish overall.

The paya soup was good and comforting. The broth had a light yet hearty body with a noticeable peppery warmth and gentle spice from the masala. That said, I would have preferred a deeper meaty and fatty richness in the broth. The paya piece itself was well cooked, with soft meat and gelatinous fat that almost melted in the mouth.

Overall, it was a very satisfying experience, and I will definitely be exploring more dishes from here.
